### Investment Memo: ONON — 12 November 2026

**Verdict**: BUY (Initiate, small size) | Conviction: **Medium**
**Price Target**: $42 (~21% upside from current $34.70)
**Time Horizon**: 12–24 months

**Investment Thesis**
On Holding is the strongest-positioned listed pure play on the only growing pocket of a flat footwear market — performance running (+13% vs. +1% category growth) — with best-in-class gross margins (62.8% FY25, ~67% underlying), a record 45.7% DTC mix, net cash, and founders who bought $10.6m of stock at the lows. The stock has de-rated ~45% from highs *while EPS grew* — this is a real-rate-driven multiple compression, not fundamental deterioration, and at 16x FY28 consensus EPS / ~0.9 PEG the market is pricing a deceleration the TAM math (~1% of a $550bn market) doesn't support. The thesis is gated on earnings quality: reported margins are flattered by CHF 52.6m of tariff refunds and a 0.7% tax rate, governance is weak, and the macro backdrop is hostile to a 2.0-beta long-duration name.

**Key Findings by Domain**
- **Macro & Sector**: Sector: premium performance niche *attractive* within a *neutral*, flat category; Nike/Puma ceding ~$8bn of scale that On is absorbing. Macro **unfavourable**: real 10Y ~2.93% with the Fed hiking (3.88%), UMich sentiment 48.1 — the worst backdrop for a high-beta compounder, and the primary cause of the de-rating. Mitigant: core CPI anchored at 2.5%, so a rate stabilisation is the re-rating trigger.
- **Geopolitical & Legal**: **Medium risk.** ~52–58% US revenue against ~90% Vietnam footwear sourcing, in a tariff regime rewritten three times in 12 months. Tariff refunds moved Q3 GM by ~570bps — policy is a top driver of reported margin. Legal exposure immaterial ($ terms); watch CBP transshipment enforcement and the CloudTec/"Swissness" class actions.
- **Value**: BUY. Net cash, ROIC 17% and rising, GM up ~700bps in four years with genuine full-price selling power. Agent's $52 DCF was re-triangulated by the Portfolio Strategist on consensus to **~$42** (25x FY27E EPS $1.725; street median PT $40.50) — ~21% upside, not 33%. Narrow moat, re-earned seasonally; bear case (~$26–28) is near the September low.
- **Growth**: BUY. 47.9% four-year CAGR; apparel +39%, APAC +31%, DTC +34% cc. But growth has halved (30%→17%), Rule of 40 is sub-threshold (~33), and Q3's beat was margin-driven on in-line revenue. FY26 consensus EPS ($1.456) looks stale vs. ~$1.57 YTD adjusted.
- **Quantitative Signals**: **SELL, low conviction** — the dissenting view. Value 18/100, momentum −6.5% (12-1), alpha −38%, Sharpe −0.40, 50% vol, R² 0.126. Offsets: clean accruals, ROIC 17%, mildly positive long-dated revisions. The tape has *not* confirmed the fundamental story; EPS beats are being sold (Q3: +40% beat, −7.5%).
- **Financial Risk**: **Moderate, decomposed.** Solvency/liquidity/credit: LOW (net cash CHF 439m, 17–21x coverage; a 30% revenue collapse is breakeven, not a credit event). FCF sustainability: MODERATE-HIGH (FCF −43% on a CHF 304m working-capital swing; margin 19.2%→8.4%). SG&A outgrowing revenue (+21% vs +17% Q3). FY25's ~0.7% tax rate flatters earnings ~20%.
- **Non-Financial Risk**: **Moderate-High.** Governance **weak and structural**: co-CEOs are also co-Chairs of a dual-class company (~59% founder voting); CEO/CFO/COO all turned over within 12 months; unexplained FY25 statutory loss of CHF 67.9m. Strong offset: founder open-market buying $10.6m at $30.67–36.64 (10.6:1 buy/sell ratio).
- **ESG**: Average/Neutral — not a thesis driver. Absolute Scope 3 rising against a conceded off-track 2030 SBT; Cyclon wind-down and the CleanCloud "Pathway 2b" caveat are greenwashing tail risks; PFAS deadlines bite the outdoor growth vector. No realised controversies, no ESG-linked debt.
- **Alternative Data**: Neutral with constructive skew. Web traffic +29.8% MoM, brand search +25% YoY and recovering, On/Hoka search ratio flat (share intact) — consistent with guided Q4 DTC acceleration. Offset: product-term searches −30% YoY; social sentiment bearish but thin.
- **Short / Contrarian View**: **⚠️ Short Analyst produced no report — an unassessed dimension.** Flagged explicitly: absence of a short thesis is not evidence of none. The implied short case from other agents: DECK-multiple compression to ~$20–25 if growth breaks to mid-single digits; tariff-refund reversal; brand-heat decay (UA/HOKA template). This gap caps position size.

**Bull Case**
- Structural share gainer in the one growing sub-segment, with pricing power proven by 66.9% underlying GM *in a promotional market* and record DTC — consensus FY29 ($5.8bn revenue, ~14% CAGR) is below what 1%→3% TAM share mechanically delivers.
- Multiple has de-rated to ~16x FY28 EPS / 16x FY26E EBITDA on consensus while fundamentals improved; a real-rate stabilisation alone recovers much of the 45% drawdown, with insider buying marking the floor.
- Operating leverage inflecting: op margin 9.1%→12.5%→~15%+ guided, with DTC mix and LightSpray as structural margin levers.

**Bear Case**
- Growth durability: 30%→17% in four quarters, wholesale softening, two guide-downs in 2026; a FY27 guide to mid-teens compresses the multiple regardless of margin quality (DECK at 8x EBITDA implies ~$20–25).
- Earnings quality: Q3 GM of 72.6% is 66.9% ex-refunds; FY25 net income flattered by a ~0.7% tax rate; FCF −43%; reported run-rate profitability is overstated.
- Exogenous macro: real 10Y at 2.93% and a hiking Fed against a 2.0-beta, 50%-vol name — cheap can stay cheap; negative 3-year Sharpe says holders have been paid nothing for the risk.

**Key Risks**
1. FY27 guidance below mid-teens or a third consecutive reset (primary thesis risk).
2. Tariff regime reversal / CBP origin enforcement on Vietnamese footwear — margin is partly a policy variable.
3. Brand-heat decay in a fad-prone category with no switching costs.
4. Governance: founder-controlled, fused CEO/Chair, untested bench, unexplained CHF 67.9m statutory loss.
5. Working-capital deterioration (DSO 47 days, inventory watch) and CHF translation headwinds.

**Portfolio Construction Note**
Initiate at **1.5% of portfolio**, scaled in three tranches: 40% now (~$34.70), 35% on a pullback to $30–31 *or* a volume reclaim of $38.62, 25% only after the Q4/FY26 print (~2-Mar-2027) confirms ≥66% underlying GM ex-refunds *and* FY27 guidance ≥20% cc. **Hard ceiling 3.0%; no purchases above $38.** If DECK is held, manage as one premium-running sleeve capped at 4% combined (pairwise correlation 0.609). Risk framework: hard floor $26.50 (break of the September low = exit); halve at −20% from cost; trim to 1.0% at $42, to 0.5% at $47–50. Thesis invalidation on any two of: FY27 guide <mid-teens, ex-refund GM <64%, SG&A > revenue growth for a third quarter, DTC < wholesale growth, inventory > sales growth, or the statutory loss left unexplained in the FY26 20-F. Fund from cash or a discretionary sleeve — **pass entirely if the book is already overweight long-duration, rate-sensitive growth.**

*Diligence gaps carried forward: no short-thesis report; FY2025 20-F risk factors not directly reviewed (FPI feed blocked); driver of the CHF 67.9m statutory loss and the CHF 304m working-capital swing unconfirmed.*

**Price $34.70 (10-Nov-26 close) · Mkt cap $11.6bn · EV $11.1bn · Beta 1.22 daily / ~2.08 effective · 49.4% ann. vol**

---

## 1. Agent Conviction Summary Table

| **Geo Legal Researcher** | **MEDIUM** | **Medium-High** | ~52–58% US revenue, ~90% footwear Vietnam. Tariff regime rewritten 3× in 12 months; **CHF 52.6m refunds = 570bps of Q3 GM**. No enforcement action; legal $ immaterial |

| **Portfolio Strategist** | **INITIATE, sized small** | **Medium** | See below |

---

## 2. Consensus Assessment: **SPLIT — but a resolvable split**

**Fundamentals: high agreement (~8 of 10 agents).** Sector, Value, Growth, Alt Data, ESG, Geo Legal and the insider tape all converge: this is a genuinely elite-margin, founder-led, net-cash franchise taking structural share, and the *business* is executing better than the *stock*.

**Return drivers: fundamental disagreement.** The split is not about the company — it is about **which variable sets the price**:
- **Fundamental camp** prices ONON off growth durability and margin convergence → BUY.
- **Macro + Quant camp** prices it off the discount rate and the tape → real 10Y at 2.93%, alpha −38%, momentum −6.5%, negative Sharpe → SELL.

**Resolution (precedence rules applied):**
1. **Macro/Quant win the *timing and sizing* argument, not the *direction* argument.** The de-rating is provably exogenous — EPS grew while the stock fell 45%. I cannot forecast real yields, so I must not size as if the re-rating is imminent. Nine months of tape says "cheap can stay cheap."
2. **The risk agents win the *quality-of-earnings* argument outright.** Non-Fin's governance finding and Fin Risk's FCF/tax-rate findings take precedence over the Value bull case — not because the business is impaired, but because **the headline numbers investors are underwriting are not the run-rate numbers.** Specifically: Q3 GM of 72.6% is 66.9% ex-refund; FY25's ~0.7% effective tax rate flatters net income ~20%; FY25 FCF fell 43% on a CHF 304m working-capital swing; SG&A is outgrowing revenue (Q3: +21% vs +17%).
3. **Governance is a permanent discount factor, not a fixable item.** Co-CEOs who co-Chair a dual-class board the minority cannot influence. This belongs in the discount rate and the position cap, permanently.
4. **Insider buying is the single most credible counterweight** — founders put $10.6m of personal capital in at $30.67–36.64 immediately after the August collapse. That is why this is Initiate and not Pass.

---

## 3. Correction to the Agent Multiples — the fair value is lower than $52

Before sizing, I re-derived valuation from the consensus base, because two agents' multiples do not reconcile with the estimate set.

| Metric | Bull-case claim | **Re-derived (consensus)** | Check |
|---|---|---|---|
| FY26E revenue | $3.56bn | **$3.562bn** | 23 analysts |
| FY26E EBITDA | (implied ~$856m) | **$686m** | 19.3% margin — matches mgmt's 19.5–20% guide ✔ |
| **EV/EBITDA FY26E** | ~12.5–13.6x | **~16.2x** | $11.15bn / $686m |
| **EV/Sales FY26E** | ~2.5–2.6x | **~3.1x** | $11.15bn / $3.562bn |
| P/E FY26E | 23.8x | **23.8x** | $34.70 / $1.456 ✔ |
| P/E FY27E / FY28E | — | **20.1x / 16.1x** | $1.725 / $2.152 |
| FY27E EBITDA | "~$1.0bn" | **$779m** | — |

**Consequence:** the Value Researcher's $52 rests partly on a FY27 EPS of $2.10 that is ~22% above consensus ($1.725), and on an EBITDA base ~30% too high. **Re-triangulating on consensus:** 25x FY27E EPS = **$43**; 16x FY27E EBITDA + net cash = **$39.50**; street median PT (12 recent notes, range $28–60) = **$40.50**.

**Adopted intrinsic value: ~$42** (base case). Bear **$26–28** (DECK-style 8x EBITDA → ~$20–25 on a broken-growth outcome; the Sept-26 low was $26.85). Bull **$50–60** *only* if FY27 guides ≥20% with a tariff-clean 66%+ GM.

**This changes the trade materially:** upside to fair value is **~+21%**, not +33%. A 21% upside against a −28% bear case is roughly **1:1 risk/reward with a ~0.75 edge-to-odds ratio** — investable at a small size, not at a core size. *Note: the reported trailing P/E 56.9x, EV/EBITDA 31.4x and P/FCF 45.8x are FX-blind, one-off-flattered artefacts and should be ignored (all agents flagged this).*

---

## 4. Position Sizing Recommendation: **1.5% of portfolio, path to 2.5% max**

**Recommendation: initiate at 1.5%; hard ceiling 3.0%; expected steady-state 2.0–2.5%.**

**Rationale — three independent constraints all point to the same number:**

| Constraint | Calculation | Implied ceiling |
|---|---|---|
| **Conviction band** (medium conviction, multiple risk flags) | Framework: 1–3% | 3.0% |
| **Volatility budget** | 49.4% ann. vol × 2.5% = **1.24% standalone portfolio vol**; at effective beta ~2.0, ~5% beta-adjusted exposure ≈ **~10% of a 12%-vol portfolio's total risk** from one name | 2.5% |
| **Kelly fraction, halved twice** | Edge/odds ≈ 20%/28% = 0.71; p≈0.75 → f\* ≈ 0.40. One-quarter Kelly for a 2.0-beta name with a 12% R² and a missing short report | ~2.5% (heavily discounted) |
| **Gap-risk tolerance** | Repeating August's −20.3% single-day event on a 2.5% position = **−50bps portfolio** | 2.5–3.0% |

**Why the sub-3% cap survives the bull case:** 87% of ONON's variance is idiosyncratic (R² 0.126). That is *good* for diversification — genuine alpha potential — but it means a 3% position behaves like a 3% *event bet*, not like 3% of market exposure. Combined with weak governance (no lever if execution slips a third time) and a policy-dependent gross margin, the sizing must be governed by downside tolerance, not by upside conviction.

---

## 5. Portfolio Fit Analysis

**Sector:** Adds to Consumer Discretionary / Apparel-Footwear. *Conditional on existing holdings:* if the portfolio already owns **DECK**, the two must be managed as a single **"premium performance running" sleeve capped at 4% combined** — DECK/ONON is the **highest pairwise correlation in the matrix (0.609)** and they are direct HOKA-vs-On competitors. If NKE/LULU are held, note ONON correlates 0.40 to each (lower than to DECK), so they are complements, not substitutes.

**Correlation structure (252d, verified):**
| Pair | ρ | Read |
|---|---|---|
| ONON–DECK | **0.609** | Binding constraint. Same sub-sector, same short thesis |
| ONON–XLY | 0.442 | Standard discretionary exposure |
| ONON–NKE / LULU | 0.405 / 0.398 | Moderate |
| ONON–SPY | **0.354** | Low; R² 0.126 → 87% idiosyncratic |

**Factor exposure — net additive to unintended tilts:**
- ❌ **Increases** high-beta growth tilt (+1.2 daily β, ~2.0 effective — a 10% index drawdown plausibly costs 20%+)
- ❌ **Increases** negative-momentum exposure (12-1 return **−6.5%**, alpha **−38%**)
- ❌ **Increases** "expensive on trailing earnings" exposure (23.8x forward is fine; the name screens bottom-quintile on realized value)
- ❌ **Reduces** portfolio quality as measured: FCF margin 8.4%, ROA 12.2%→7.8%, F-score 7/9
- ✅ **Reduces** concentration of market beta (low R²)
- ➖ Zero dividend — no income contribution; zero buyback despite CHF 1.4bn cash and a CHF 1bn authorization

**Net:** acceptable only as a **satellite growth position**, funded from cash or from an existing discretionary/momentum sleeve — **not** by adding to an already growth-heavy book. If the portfolio is currently overweight long-duration, rate-sensitive growth, this position should be **passed on**, regardless of the 21% upside.

**Currency/domicile:** CHF-reporting, USD-listed, ~52–58% US revenue, 90% Vietnam sourcing. Adds USD/CHF translation risk and a non-diversifiable tariff-policy exposure. The USD firming (+3.2% broad since Sept 1, USD/CHF 0.8192) is a modest translation tailwind that partially self-hedges (COGS is USD-denominated).

---

## 6. Entry Strategy: **Scale in over three tranches — do not buy at once**

The tape does not support a full-size entry today: the stock rallied **+25% from $26.85 (10-Sep) to $38.62 (4-Nov)**, then **failed there and gapped −7.5%** on a tariff-refund-dependent beat, closing at $34.70 on 24.7m shares. It sits mid-range with negative 12-1 momentum and no confirmation.

| Tranche | Size | Trigger | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| **T1 — now** | **40%** (~0.6%) | At market ~$34.70 | The fundamental discount is real; own *some* before the event risk |
| **T2 — on weakness or confirmation** | **35%** (~0.5%) | Pullback to **$30–31** (re-entry into the Aug gap zone) **or** a decisive reclaim of **$38.62** on volume | Buy the liquidity event, not the drift. Either side of the range is informative |
| **T3 — evidence-gated** | **25%** (~0.4%) | After the **Q4/FY26 print (~2-Mar-2027)**: underlying GM ≥66% *excluding* refunds **and** FY27 guide ≥20% cc | This is the one thing every agent asked for. Do not pre-pay for it |

**Hard rule: no purchases above $38.** At 90% of my $42 intrinsic value the risk/reward is flat, and above ~$42 the position is a Hold/trim regardless of narrative.

---

## 7. Risk Management Rules

**Stop-loss: do not use a tight price stop.** A 49%-vol name with two −11%/−20% single-day gaps (25-Mar, 11-Aug) will stop you out on noise. Use these instead:

| Rule | Level / Condition | Action |
|---|---|---|
| **Hard price floor** | **$26.50** (Sept-26 low, −24% from spot) | Exit. A break of the capitulation low with no fundamental repair means the bear case ($20–25) is in play |
| **Position-loss circuit-breaker** | −20% from average cost | Halve the position and re-underwrite; do not average down without a clean print |
| **Sizing drift** | Position >3.0% of portfolio from appreciation | Trim back to 2.5% mechanically |

**Thesis invalidation — any two of these = exit, regardless of price:**
1. FY27 revenue guided **below mid-teens**, or a third consecutive guide-down.
2. **Underlying (ex-refund) gross margin below 64%** — the full-price selling story is broken, and margin is the *entire* moat proof.
3. **SG&A grows faster than revenue for a third consecutive quarter** (the operating-leverage thesis inverts to permanent).
4. **DTC growth decelerates below wholesale** growth — the highest-quality demand indicator reverses.
5. **Inventory grows faster than sales** in any reported period (invalidates "healthy full-price sell-through").
6. A **CBP transshipment/origin penalty** on Vietnamese footwear, a formal greenwashing action (EU Green Claims / state AG) targeting CleanCloud or "preferred materials", or a forced-labour finding in the Vietnam chain.
7. **Founders reduce stakes**, or the 100% living-wage target is missed again.
8. **2025 statutory loss (CHF 67.9m) is not satisfactorily explained** in the FY26 20-F — this is an open diligence item and an accounting-quality tripwire.

**Trim triggers:**
- **$38 (90% of IV):** halt all accumulation; if the position has grown above 2.5%, trim to 2.5%.
- **$42 (fair value):** trim to **1.0%** — take the re-rating, keep a stub for the FY28–29 TAM compounding.
- **$47–50:** trim to **0.5%** core. Only hold through this level if FY27 revenue is tracking ≥20% *and* GM is ≥66% without refunds.

**Monitoring calendar:** Q4/FY26 results **~2-Mar-2027** (a duplicate 18-Mar listing exists — confirm the date); FY2026 20-F (for the CHF 67.9m statutory loss and the commentary on the CHF 304m working-capital swing); FY26 Impact Report (absolute Scope 3, Tier 2 renewables, living-wage 77%→100%); CBP/USTR actions on Vietnam origin; the "Swissness" and CloudTec class actions.

---

## 8. Final Portfolio Action: **INITIATE — 1.5%, scaled to 2.5–3% on evidence**

**One line:** Buy the business, rent the multiple, cap the size. ONON is the strongest-positioned pure play on the only growing pocket of a flat footwear market — 62.8%→66.9% gross margins, record DTC, ~1% of a $550bn TAM, net cash, founders buying at the lows — but it is priced by a real-rate shock it does not control, reports earnings flattered by tariff refunds and a 0.7% tax rate, and is governed by a founder

# Sector Brief: On Holding AG (ONON)
## Industry: Apparel – Footwear & Accessories | Sector: Consumer Cyclical | Domicile: Switzerland

---

## 1. Sector Overview

ONON competes in the global **athletic footwear and performance apparel** market, valued at roughly **$94.5bn in 2026 and forecast to reach $120.2bn by 2030 (~6.2% CAGR)**. The headline market is **mature and slow-growing**: US footwear retail sales grew only **+1% in H1 2026**, and Circana expects the US industry to close 2026 "generally flat." However, the market is bifurcating sharply — **performance footwear rose +6% and running shoes +13%** in H1 2026 while fashion/lifestyle sneakers stagnated. Concentration is high at the top (Nike, adidas, Deckers/HOKA, Puma, New Balance) but **eroding**: Nike's revenue has fallen from $51.4bn (FY2024) to $46.4bn (FY2026) and Puma's from €8.8bn to €7.0bn, ceding ~$8bn of combined scale that challengers are absorbing. Barriers are **brand-led rather than capital-led** — contract manufacturing in Vietnam/Indonesia/China keeps capex low, so share shifts can happen fast, as HOKA and On have both proven.

---

## 2. Key Tailwinds

- **Performance running is the one genuinely growing pocket of a flat market.** Running footwear +13% and performance +6% in US H1 2026 vs. total market +1%. On is the purest listed play on this shift, with running-derived credibility (Cloudsurfer 3, Cloudtilt) rather than retro-fashion exposure.
- **Premiumisation and full-price selling.** ONON held full-price sales "in a promotional market" (Q3 2026) and lifted gross margin guidance. Gross margin reached **62.8% in FY2025** — roughly **1,090bps above the peer median of 51.9%** — evidence that brand heat, not discounting, is driving volume.
- **Share capture from incumbents plus channel and geographic whitespace.** Nike and Puma are both shrinking (Puma revenue −20.5% in FY2025, operating margin −5.2%), releasing shelf space in run specialty and general sporting goods. On is still early in APAC/China and in apparel attach, where DTC mix gains carry structurally higher margin.

---

## 3. Key Headwinds

- **Tariffs and input-cost/FX pressure.** US tariffs on Southeast Asian footwear supply chains remain the sector's biggest swing factor; On's Q3 2026 gross margin of **72.6%** was materially flattered by **tariff refunds**, so that level is not a clean run-rate. A stronger CHF also translates offshore earnings down.
- **Selective consumer spending in a discretionary category.** Circana's flat-2026 outlook reflects consumers "making intentional purchasing decisions." Footwear is a deferrable purchase — a weak labour market or tariff-driven price increases at the $150–180 price point are direct volume risks.
- **Promotional risk from incumbent clean-up.** Nike (8.2% operating margin, down from 13.6% in FY2024), Puma (loss-making) and Crox (−1.5% revenue, net loss) all have inventory and margin repair ahead. Their markdowns can compress the whole category's pricing, and On's premium positioning is only defensible while discounting stays contained.

---

## 4. Peer Comparison Table

| PUMSY (Puma) | Dec-25 | €7,008m | −20.5% | 39.6% | −5.2% | −8.8% |
| **Peer median (ex-ONON)** | — | — | **+0.4%** | **51.9%** | **8.1%** | 6.1% |

This is a high-quality, founder-led, net-cash compounder with widening gross margins and a genuine (if fashion-sensitive) brand, trading at ~12.5x EV/EBITDA and ~21x normalised earnings for ~17% growth. That combination is rare and offers a ~33% discount to base-case intrinsic value of ~$52.

**Bottom line:** A better business than its chart suggests, at a price that finally asks little of it. **The core finding: On is decarbonising per unit while growing so fast that absolute emissions keep rising, and its own report concedes it is off-track against its 2030 science-based target.**

- **FY2024:** absolute Scope 1+2 emissions **+13% y/y**; Scope 3 *economic-intensity* emissions **+3% y/y**. On's mitigation: emissions grew slower than production volumes, and average emissions per product fell.

Positives (genuine, not marketing):
- **100% renewable electricity** for offices and stores achieved (2024).
- **Coal phased out** across Tier 1 suppliers (2024) — a meaningful, verifiable Scope 3 intervention that many peers have not completed.

**Hidden liability to flag:** On's *own* CleanCloud lifecycle documentation references a "Pathway 2b (Cut-off Approach)" scenario in which the CleanCloud material's carbon footprint is **higher than fossil-based EVA**. ## 8. ESG Investment Implication: **NEUTRAL**

**ESG is not a thesis driver for ONON — it is a monitorable tail risk and a modest cost-of-capital consideration. It is not a reason to own or avoid the stock.**

**Why neutral rather than negative:**
- No realised controversies, fines, or litigation — the ESG "accident waiting to happen" is absent.
- No ESG-linked debt, so no financing covenant risk.
- Compliance costs are real but small relative to a 62.8% gross margin and CHF 1.89bn gross profit.
- Traceability and supplier-engagement infrastructure is a genuine relative advantage entering the ESPR/CSRD era.

**Why neutral rather than positive:**
- Absolute emissions are rising against a public science-based target in a business growing >25%/yr. The math does not close without Tier 2 renewable procurement that On has not yet demonstrated at scale.
- Governance has moved *backwards* in 2026: professional CEO out, founders back in as Co-CEOs **and** Co-Chairs of a dual-class company. Governance-screened and SFDR Article 8/9 funds face structural limits on position size.
- PFAS deadlines (CA 2025/2027, EU 2027) land directly on the outdoor/waterproof growth vector.

**What would move us to Negative:** a formal greenwashing challenge (EU Green Claims, state AG, or NGO complaint) targeting CleanCloud® or "preferred materials"; disclosure of a forced-labour finding in the Vietnam chain; or FY2026 disclosure that absolute Scope 3 rose again with the 2030 SBT formally abandoned or restated.

**What would move us to Positive:** verified Tier 2 renewable energy contracting with quantified absolute-emissions decline (not just intensity); achievement of the 100% living-wage target in 2026; LightSpray™ scaled beyond pilot volumes; and introduction of ESG metrics into executive variable pay.

**Monitoring checklist for the FY2026 Impact Report:** (1) absolute tCO₂e, not just per-product intensity; (2) Tier 2 renewable energy %; (3) living-wage coverage — did the 77%→100% roll-forward hold?; (4) PFAS-free certification across outdoor range; (5) any change to Class B voting rights or board independence following the 2026 AGM's approved Class B conversion.
